title: Neural circuit mechanisms underlying context-specific halting in Drosophila
quote: We identified split-Gal4 reagents that targeted FG, BB and BRK with little to no ectopic expression and drove robust halting
mapping_basis: Kit maps BB/bluebell to DNg60 or DNxn073 (ambiguous); paper's Supp. Table 3 identifies BB as FlyWire type DNg60, which the kit lists as the flywire type of MANC DNxn073 (MANC DNg60 corresponds to FlyWire DNge096), so DNxn073 chosen.
stimulation: red light 630 nm pulsed 50 Hz (5 ms pulses), 0.038 mW/mm2 at arena surface, 10 s ON / 50 s OFF x5
sensory_condition: free walking in 44 mm bowl arena, IR backlight, dim green background light
penetrance: distance and rotation significantly reduced vs empty-split control (P<0.001)
notes: FlyTracker centroid velocity only (no leg tracking). BB halting is weaker than FG/BRK (distance reduced, not abolished). The same line appears in the Extended Data Fig. 1a screen heatmap.

title: Neural circuit mechanisms underlying context-specific halting in Drosophila
source_locator: Fig. 1g; Extended Data Fig. 3c-e; Supplementary Video 1
quote: BB drove stationary periods interspersed with slow walking and allowed more leg movements
mapping_basis: Kit maps BB/bluebell to DNg60 or DNxn073 (ambiguous); paper's Supp. Table 3 identifies BB as FlyWire type DNg60, which the kit lists as the flywire type of MANC DNxn073 (MANC DNg60 corresponds to FlyWire DNge096), so DNxn073 chosen.
stimulation: 625 nm red light via optic fibre, 66 Hz, ~0.04 mW/mm2, 3 s per trial, up to 10 trials triggered closed-loop on forward velocity
sensory_condition: tethered on air-supported ball at 32 C, starved 6-9 h, walking >1 mm/s before stimulation
coordination_notes: flies often took a few steps before halting; halts interspersed with slow walking
notes: 3D leg kinematics (8-camera, DeepLabCut/Anipose). This is the weakest of the three halt phenotypes: stepping stops but is interrupted by slow walking.

title: Neural circuit mechanisms underlying context-specific halting in Drosophila

quote: Although BPN + FG + BB coactivated flies decreased forward walking it was interspersed with intermittent jumps possibly due to ectopic expression in the VNC
mapping_basis: Foxglove is FlyWire CB0890 in the paper's Supp. Table 3 with no MANC match; not in kit name maps.
stimulation: red light 630 nm pulsed 50 Hz (5 ms pulses), 0.038 mW/mm2 at arena surface, 10 s ON / 50 s OFF x5
sensory_condition: free walking in 44 mm bowl arena
other_cell_types: 2 ectopic cells incl. VNC expression (Extended Data Fig. 4a)
penetrance: distance quantification deemed unreliable by authors
notes: Co-activation experiment. Velocity rises briefly at onset then returns toward baseline (Fig. 2c magenta), with intermittent jumps. The outcome is mixed, so legs are coded unclear.

title: Neural circuit mechanisms underlying context-specific halting in Drosophila
quote: However, decapitated MDN + BRK stimulated flies remained stationary
mapping_basis: The paper's name 'MDN' is a MANC type in type_list.csv (one type).
stimulation: 3 s red light, 66 Hz, 0.04 mW/mm2, 10 trials of 7 s
sensory_condition: decapitated, tethered on air-supported ball
coordination_notes: front-leg Fe-Ti locked; rarely reached the swing initiation zone, rarely lifted
penetrance: SIZ count and % swings in SIZ reduced vs MDN alone (P<0.001)
notes: Co-activation experiment with the ascending brake neuron BRK (not a DN). 3D leg kinematics: 26 front-leg swings vs 385 for MDN alone.

title: Neural circuit mechanisms underlying context-specific halting in Drosophila
source_locator: Fig. 4e-j (BDN2 + BRK, decapitated); Extended Data Fig. 6g,h; Supplementary Video 5
quote: Despite this difference, coactivation with BRK interrupted forward walking
mapping_basis: Kit synonym BDN2 -> DNg100 (unambiguous).
stimulation: 3 s red light, 66 Hz; per-fly intensity chosen from 0.01-0.058 mW/mm2
sensory_condition: decapitated, tethered on air-supported ball; flies 10-12 days old
coordination_notes: front-leg Fe-Ti resisted flexion; long dwell in swing initiation zone without swinging
penetrance: ball velocity about 0 (Fig. 4e); 128 front-leg swings vs 2598 for BDN2 alone
notes: Co-activation experiment with BRK (not a DN). 3D leg kinematics. Methods: if BDN2 expression is weak, BRK dominates and the legs do not move.
